# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 74 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 74 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_074_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 74 opens the longest section of the Shepherd of Hermas — Similitude 9, which runs through chapter 110. This is the capstone vision, reinterpreting and expanding the tower-vision from the early Visions section. The angel explicitly states in 74:1 that he is now going to reveal what the Holy Spirit said "in the form of the church" — i.e., the woman-church figure who appeared in the Visions is now identified as the Holy Spirit, who is identified as the Son of God. This is the same adoptionist/Spirit-christology found in Similitude 5.

The location is Arcadia (*eis tēn Arkadian*) — an unexpected geographic specificity. This is likely symbolic (Arcadia as a pastoral ideal landscape) rather than topographic. All three agents preserve "Arcadia."

The twelve mountains represent twelve different nations or peoples who have heard the gospel — they will be interpreted later in Similitude 9. Their different appearances (black/barren/thorny/partly withered/rugged/cracked/lush/spring-filled/desert/shaded/fruit-laden/white) correspond to twelve different types of believers and their moral states. This is a more elaborate and cosmopolitan version of the rod-typology.

The seventh mountain — "cheerful vegetation," cattle and birds multiplying — stands out as paradisiacal. EMET has "smiling vegetation," LOGOS "cheerful vegetation." The Greek *hilaros* means "cheerful/joyful" — "cheerful" is precise; "smiling" is a striking metaphor but less standard.

The twelfth mountain is *leukos holē* ("entirely white") with an appearance described as *hilaros* (cheerful/radiant/joyful). This mountain is clearly associated with purity and glory. LOGOS adds "radiant and joyful" which captures both *leukos* (white/bright) and *hilaros*.

---

## Similitude 9, Part 1 — The Great Plain and the Twelve Mountains

**74:1** After I had written down the commandments and similitudes of the shepherd, the angel of repentance, he came to me and said: "I want to show you all the things the Holy Spirit spoke with you in the form of the church. For that Spirit is the Son of God."

**74:2** "For you were weak in the flesh, and the truth had not yet been explained to you. Speak with the Power and it will come to you more clearly, because that Power is strong and divine and belongs to glorious and mighty virtue."

**74:3** I said to him: "Lord, I beg you to show me all the things you promised to show me." And he led me to Arcadia, to a certain hill, and seated me on the hill. And he himself stood before me.

**74:4** And I saw a great plain, and around the plain twelve mountains, each having a different form. The first mountain was all black rock. The second was bare, with no vegetation at all. The third was full of thorns and brambles. The fourth had vegetation that was half-withered — the upper parts of the plants were green but the roots were dry, and some plants were withered because the sun had scorched them. The fifth mountain had green grass but was rugged. The sixth mountain was full of clefts, some small and some large, and in the clefts there was grass.

**74:5** The seventh mountain had cheerful vegetation, and the whole mountain was blooming, and all kinds of cattle and birds fed on that mountain; and the more the cattle and birds fed, the more the vegetation flourished. The eighth mountain was full of springs, and every kind of creature of the Lord drank from those springs.

**74:6** The ninth mountain had no water whatsoever and was entirely a wilderness, and it was full of wild beasts and deadly reptiles that destroyed human beings. The tenth mountain had great trees and was entirely shaded, and beneath those trees sheep lay resting and ruminating.

**74:7** The eleventh mountain was densely covered with trees, and those trees were laden with various fruits, so that anyone who saw them would desire to eat of their fruits. The twelfth mountain was entirely white, and its appearance was radiant and joyful, and the mountain was very beautiful in form.

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
